author: Evangeline Lilly
title: The Heavy Blanket of Heartbreak
text:
Approx. 8min read
The last time I wrote, I was contemplating abandoning my birthday trip to South Africa. I have wanted to go on a silent retreat for at least a decade now, but life was just life-ing and the opportunity never seemed to present itself. So, when I was exclusively invited to go on a ten-day, no tent, no vehicle, wild game, silent, African walkabout with an intimate group of like-minded souls…I jumped. Then, life started life-ing again and I almost bailed.
You might be happy to know that I’m in South Africa now, out in the open wilds, sleeping under the stars and carrying everything I need on my back. I would love to tell you how it’s going, what it’s like out here, if we’ve had any animal encounters…everything. But I can’t. Because I’ve pre-scheduled this article to drop while I don’t have a toilet to use, let alone a digital device.
Before I left, I was contemplating heartbreak on two different scales: both the personal and the political. As you know, I have recently gone through a heart-wrenching break-up, and that break-up happened to coincide with the world I grew up in becoming ever more desperate and threatening. And so, on two different levels, I was (and am) enduring tremendous heartbreak, and noticing that hearts can break in many different ways.
…hearts can break in many different ways.
